item.title: Former Barcelona forward urges patience with Real Madrid’s South American stars
item.description: Former Barcelona forward urges patience with Real Madrid’s South American stars Vitor Roque has been enjoying life ever since his return to Brazil. Since joining Palmeiras in 2025, the forward has racked up 29 goals, and his market value has also gone up. This comes on the back of a disastrous spell at Barcelona, where the player struggled to prove himself and eventually left the club permanently in 2025. In light of his success, the former Barcelona forward was recently asked about the lack of patience from European clubs when it comes to talents from South America. Vitor Roque on Endrick and Mastantuono Roque believes players like Endrick need more time. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) When asked about the South American talents, the interviewer particularly referenced two Real Madrid players: Endrick and Franco Mastantuono. Both players had joined Real Madrid in the recent past. While Mastantuono had to settle for a loan at Fiorentina, Endrick is also struggling with a lack of game time despite being a part of Jose Mourinho’s setup this season. Keeping that in mind, Roque urged more patience with these players. “People believe that young people arrive and we have to start playing 100%, giving everything, doing our best football, but it is not. It takes patience. Sometimes we don’t have the adaptation time we need,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). The former Barcelona forward pointed out how language and culture can also be a problem for young South American stars. “We are very young and speaking a new language is very difficult. Sometimes it is important to have the support of the coach and I when I went to Barcelona I did not have it. They barely talked to me, you know? “So I think you have to keep that in mind and a lot of people don’t see it that way, they think you have to be prepared from the first minute ,” he added. What’s next for Endrick and Mastantuono? Mastantuono’s fate will be decided at the end of the season. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Fortunately, it appears Real Madrid are ready to bide their time with both Endrick and Mastantuono. Especially in the case of Endrick, the club have not shown any indication of permanently parting ways with the forward. They are, in fact, ready to block a January exit for the Brazilian international, who is rated highly by coach Mourinho. As for Mastantuono, the Argentine has shown glimpses of his talents at Fiorentina. But unless he breaks out in a big way like Nico Paz, it is unlikely Real Madrid will want to make him a part of the first-team setup next season.

item.title: Atlético beat Viking 2-0 as both strikers score, but Sørloth injury hits Barcelona trip
item.description: Atlético beat Viking 2-0 as both strikers score, but Sørloth injury hits Barcelona trip Alexander Sørloth and Julián Álvarez both ended goal droughts as Atlético Madrid beat Viking FK 2-0 to reach seven points in the Champions League. Sørloth's muscle injury now adds to an injury list that already includes Lookman, just as Atlético face Barcelona and PSV. Atlético Madrid’s win over Viking FK revived their hopes of a direct top-eight finish. Three league-phase games remain, and one of them is away to PSV. Both of Simeone’s leading strikers found the net. Yet the night also added a new name to the injury list. Sørloth broke the deadlock by firing in a pass from Alejandro Grimaldo. Five minutes later, Álvarez’s free-kick crept in at the near post. It was his 27th goal in the Champions League. It was also his first Champions League goal at the Metropolitano in 210 days. The strike was his third of the 2026-27 season: one in LaLiga and two in Europe. Grimaldo was named Player of the Match. Viking defender Henrik Falchener was sent off late in the game. Win steadies a European campaign that stalled against Bayern The result follows an uneven league phase. Atlético opened with a 2-1 defeat at Liverpool. They then beat Manchester United 2-0 at home. A 1-1 draw at Stuttgart followed. Bayern München then won 0-2 at the Metropolitano on 3 November. That home defeat was unusual. Before kick-off against Viking, Atlético had won 11 of their previous 14 home matches in the group stage or league phase. They lost the other three. The victory over the Norwegian side returned them to winning ways in front of their own supporters. The mood inside the stadium was not entirely positive, however. Some home fans whistled Álvarez when he was substituted, even though he had scored. Sørloth injury leaves Simeone short before Barcelona and PSV Sørloth went off limping after 71 minutes. He had taken a heavy knock against the post and left the field with an overload, the club said on 26 November. No date has been set for his return. He will do physiotherapy and gym rehabilitation. The expected absence is significant. ESPN Deportes expects him to miss at least the games against Elche, Barcelona, Real Betis, Valencia and PSV. That would rule him out of the visit to Eindhoven. His injury adds to a list that already includes Lookman. The forward has a high-grade knee sprain. Simeone is therefore short of attacking options for a demanding run of fixtures. The first major test comes at the Spotify Camp Nou on Wednesday 2 December, with kick-off at 20:30 GMT (21:30 in Spain). Viking host Feyenoord on 8 December. Atlético’s next Champions League game follows a day later, away to PSV Eindhoven on 9 December. item.title: ‘He just…’ – Luka Doncic addresses throwing wristband at Spurs fan before post-game altercation
item.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic found himself in some post-game controversy after the team’s 99-96 loss to the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Cup. Doncic had a mixed night in which he stuffed the box score with 31 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals. However, he also took 31 shots, shot 1-13 from three-point range, and left with a high-profile loss to their rivals in San Antonio. As Doncic left the court, he appeared to throw his wristband at some Spurs fans courtside, who did not appreciate the gesture. As Doncic went to pick the wristband back up, a fan shoved him back, leading to a highly contentious postgame moment. Luka Doncic addresses what went down in post-game shove with Spurs fan Doncic spoke to the media after the game and explained what went down, revealing that this is something he does every game, and he got shoved by the fan when he heard them say they didn’t want it and went to retrieve it. “I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn’t want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else.” Anyone who has seen Doncic play in Dallas or Los Angeles knows he does throw his wristbands at fans after the game, usually because they want to take it home with them as memorabilia. Mavericks fan and the lead producer for LeBron James’ ‘Mind the Game’ podcast, Jason Gallagher , revealed that Doncic has done the same towards his child, but in a way that was always considered Doncic being charitable with fans. “He nonchalantly throws wristbands/headbands at fans all the time. My kid has one! Tons of players do that. It sure looks like he didn’t like what this woman said, so he went back and got it from a fan who didn’t want it. Then the dork shoved him lol.” Doncic seemed to aggressively throw the wristband, which went low and hit the woman that the Spurs fan presumably came to the game with, leading to the fan’s aggressive response when Doncic approached them to get the wristband back. The heightened tensions of this early-season marquee clash between Doncic and Victor Wembanyama’s Spurs seemed to have fans on edge, especially as this was a couple in Spurs jerseys who probably did not want Doncic’s wristband anyway, and disagreed with him throwing it towards them. item.title: Thioune concedes Bremen fortunate to draw Gladbach as West Ham loanee Füllkrug discusses potential red card incident
item.description: Thioune concedes Bremen fortunate to draw Gladbach as West Ham loanee Füllkrug discusses potential red card incident With 13 points from their first five Weserstadion encounters, sixth-placed Werder Bremen were the overwhelming favorites against cellar-dwellers Borussia Mönchengladbach on Friday. However, it took two goals after the 85th-minute mark to maintain their unbeaten home record. “Today, we got some entertaining football," Daniel Thioune started his post-match interview with Sky Sports on a positive note. "In the end, you have to be happy if you equalize. Gladbach could have wrapped up the game earlier. “We even had a chance to make it 4-3 at the end, that's crazy. That would have been too much. If you get a point based on your mentality, I'm satisfied." Thioune added regarding Cedric Itten’s missed chance after Niclas Füllkrug's injury-time equalizer. The Germany international extended his lead at the top of the scoring chart with his 11th strike since coming back to Bremen on an initial loan deal. The 33-year-old has 14 goals in all competitions, including scoring in every game at Weserstadion. “I don't think Gladbach quite deserves their position in the table,” Füllkrug praised the opposing team after the match. “The last few games have always been close. They played well against Dortmund, and they played well again today, giving us some problems.” Despite the late turnaround, the ex-BVB man wasn't satisfied with their own performance. “When you play the way we have been, expectations rise for yourself. Of course, I'm disappointed. We were far too sloppy, and lost possession far too often. We left room for improvement there today. We have to be honest about that." Füllkrug was fortunate to repeat his Dortmund heroics because Felix Zwayer could've easily sent him off for a second booking at the hour mark. For the West Ham loanee, it was best to leave that for the professionals. “I wanted to play the ball with the toe, I don't know if that was a yellow. I have no idea about that,” Füllkrug said about his challenge on Philipp Sander inside Gladbach's penalty box. “The referee has to decide that. A lot of little things were called against us. We take it as it comes. And now it turned out that I was allowed to play the whole game – great!" Werder Bremen's managing director Clemens Fritz also echoed Thioune and Füllkrug's dissatisfaction with the performance. “We didn’t play well today. We struggled to get into the game, were too passive and made a lot of mistakes. We were nowhere near our best today, but we still managed to fight back. All things considered, we have to be satisfied with a point because our performance wasn’t good enough to beat Gladbach.” the former defender said after the game.

item.title: ‘My stance is...’: Patrick Queen shares what his relationship with Aaron Rodgers is like now
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images The Aaron Rodgers situation has made this a very difficult week for the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback fell out with coach Mike McCarthy, then went on the Pat McAfee Show and had a go at him before being released by the organisation. Rodgers was a very popular teammate inside the locker room, so there have been theories on how the players would react to his behaviour following his exit. For Patrick Queen, however, there is no difference. Patrick Queen says his stance on Aaron Rodgers has not changed When there is a big split like in the case of Rodgers and McCarthy in the locker room, people would usually take sides. However, it looks like the Steelers have handled things brilliantly. On Friday, Pittsburgh produced one of their best performances of the season to beat the Denver Broncos 27-5. They were absolutely amazing. However, while speaking to the media after the game, several players showed their support for both parties. Queen is one such player, and he has spoken about his relationship with Rodgers now. He told Jenna Harner: “My stance is not going to change against Aaron. I love Aaron to death. Probably one of the coolest teammates I’ve ever had, just from the few conversations that we had. “My stance is not going to change on that. I don’t think anybody’s stance has changed on that.” That is the perfect way to handle the situation. Nobody should hate Rodgers because of the way he left, and at the same time, nobody should turn their back on coach McCarthy either. The Steelers showed on the field against the Broncos that they are fully behind their coach, and their relationship with Rodgers remains unaffected as well. The saga is well and truly over now, and it’s time for everyone to move on. item.title: 1 extremely early Canucks trade candidate not named Elias Pettersson
item.description: Bob Frid-Imagn Images 1 extremely early Canucks trade candidate not named Elias Pettersson appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Vancouver Canucks are not doing well on the ice in 2026-27. However, this was an expected outcome. The Canucks have committed to a full rebuild, which has led to trade rumors around the likes of Elias Pettersson . Rebuilds can be a pain, of course. Ask the Detroit Red Wings how things are going right now. Vancouver is currently dead last in the NHL at this time. They are the only team in the league with fewer than 15 points as of November 28th. They have lost three games in a row and seven of their last 10. It’s not a fun time to be a Canucks fan. A lot of speculation this season will center on the core veterans. Pettersson has seemingly found his stride again, producing 23 points in his first 24 games this season. He is going to dominate Canucks trade rumors throughout the entirety of the season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He won’t be the only one mentioned, though. Brock Boeser leads the team in points . Jake DeBrusk has a solid track record of offensive success. Paul Cotter could be a decent depth piece as well. There are a lot of possibilities on the trade market for Vancouver this season. And they don’t need to rush things, either. A lot of their prime trade candidates are locked up long term. They can play the waiting game a bit before making their move. In saying this, there is one player who should be considered for a trade this season. He is one of the team’s stars, but he is also a valuable asset. It would be wise for Vancouver to at least gauge his market this year. Canucks’ Filip Hronek would attract trade interest Simon Fearn-Imagn Images In 2023, the Canucks took a big swing . They traded a first-round pick and a second-round pick to the Red Wings for Filip Hronek. It was a huge move at the time. Hronek showed promise as an offensive defenseman. He was also in his mid-20s and was about to play next to Quinn Hughes. Suffice it to say, things didn’t work out in the long term, at least as far as the team’s success is concerned. Hughes was traded by the Canucks last winter, and Vancouver entered its rebuild after one playoff run. Hronek has held up his end of the bargain, though. In 255 games with Vancouver, he has scored 19 goals and 148 points. He is producing at a higher points-per-game rate than he did in Detroit, and in 50 fewer games. His offensive ability is the same, if not better, than it was when he was with the Red Wings. Why would Vancouver trade him then? It’s simple. Hronek is about to enter his 30s, and he is on a long-term contract. The Canucks are unlikely to contend anytime soon. It would be well worth trading him for future assets that aid the rebuild. Hronek is a clear top-four defenseman who can spark his team from the blueline. There are a number of contenders who would love to have someone like him on the back end.

item.title: 'I am not nice!' - Mauricio Pochettino bites back at 'Argentinian dog' claims and warns Man Utd squad of his 'strong' side
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-SPORTING-MAN UTD - AFP Mauricio Pochettino has dismissed suggestions that he has become "too nice" since taking over at Manchester United, insisting he still possesses the aggressive edge that defined his time at Tottenham. The Argentine manager warned his squad that he is prepared to be strong and demanding as he attempts to overhaul the culture at Carrington. Redknapp questions Pochettino's edge at Old Trafford Former England midfielder Jamie Redknapp sparked the debate on The Overlap with Tim Sherwood, claiming the 54-year-old had lost the edge he showed at Southampton and Tottenham. Unprompted during Friday's press conference, Pochettino mounted a firm defence of his methods. He arrived a week ago with United stranded in the Premier League relegation zone after a dismal start. Pochettino draws line between 'nice' and good Redknapp contrasted Pochettino's past intensity with his relaxed demeanour at United. "When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked to me like he had that Argentinian dog in him," Redknapp said. "I look at him now and he's high fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice, I do." Pochettino rejected that view, insisting observers had misread his approach. "Do not misunderstand my words," Pochettino said. "Sometimes we are confusing two words that mean maybe something similar; nice and good. "I am not nice. I am not nice. We have to be good. That is a different thing," he insisted. "I am not nice. I am trying to be good. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. These two things are different." Longer sessions and 14-hour days to fix United's slump Pochettino has already lengthened training sessions beyond Michael Carrick's routine, though he knows rebuilding confidence amid fierce scrutiny is vital. "I think it's easy for us because we arrived one week ago," Pochettino said. "It's easy to arrive here with full energy and be positive and try to build that belief that we need. But of course for the players it's so tough because we cannot go away from all that noise that is around this football club. It's not only in this football club. It's in every single club that is not performing well. That is why it's so tough for the players." His relentless workload has even delayed a meeting with managerial role model Sir Alex Ferguson. "I didn't have the opportunity," Pochettino added. "I send all my admiration and love to him and I promise I will send a text. Look, it's not to say nothing. It's 12, 13, 14 hours spent here in the training ground and I didn't have time. You know, we are so fully focused on trying to provide everything, to start to improve our performances." item.title: WWE Star Bronson Reed Dies at 38 Weeks After He Was Thrown Off a Stage Through Tables
item.description: Bronson Reed/Insatgram WWE star Bronson Reed , whose real name was Jermaine Haley , has died. He was 38. WWE announced that he died on Friday, November 27, due to “medical complications,” but did not provide further details. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague,” the company said in a statement. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as all his friends, co-workers and fans.” His sudden death comes just three weeks after he was badly hurt in the ring. During WWE’s Crown Jewel event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on November 7, Reed was part of an angle during the World Tag Team Championship match in which Oba Femi slammed him off the stage and through a stack of tables, Uncrowned reported. Reed reportedly suffered multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney. He remained in a hospital in Saudi Arabia for more than a week, then underwent surgery and returned home to continue his recovery. The Crown Jewel event turned out to be his final WWE appearance. WWE has not said whether his injuries were connected to his death. Born in 1988 in Adelaide, South Australia, Reed grew up playing rugby and basketball but was drawn to professional wrestling from a young age. He made his in-ring debut in 2007 and spent years competing on the independent circuit in Australia and abroad, often under the name Jonah Rock. He first signed with WWE in 2019, reporting to its developmental brand, NXT, where he won the NXT North American Championship. After being released in 2021 amid budget cuts, he returned to the company and made his main roster debut in 2022. Reed went on to win the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in 2024 and most recently was part of the stable The Vision. item.title: Xabi Alonso reflects on the predictably tragic consequences of his own decisions
item.description: NOTTINGHAM, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 27: Xabi Alonso, Manager of Chelsea, looks dejected after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Nottingham Forest FC and Chelsea FC at City Ground on November 27, 2026 in Nottingham, England. (Photo by Gareth Copley/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the week that he had had, there was surely no way Wesley Fofana was going to play, let alone start Chelsea’s match against Nottingham Forest last night, right? Even if we (somehow) ignored his generally poor performances on the pitch, after all the drama stemming from his unsanctioned interview with a podcast, including the visceral negative reaction from most of the fanbase regarding his comments about his penalty miss and financial motivations, there was surely just one, and only one obvious choice to make regarding his selection. Don’t. Just don’t. Just leave him out, for his sake and all of ours. Protect him from us, and save us from him. Win-win. Alas, Xabi Alonso decided to do something inexplicable. Fofana started at center back. And just to make matters even more interesting, he was partnered by Moisés Caicedo. (In fairness, Caicedo did well enough, though he’s very much needed in midfield so this was also a net-negative.) The travelling “support” made their feelings known loud and clear even before Fofana gave away a penalty early in the second half. Mercifully, he was soon after finally spared any further blushes. He surely cannot play for us again — or at least not for a good long while, until things settle down and become “normal”-ish for him. Though I suppose the manager might surprise us again, and not in a good way. Alonso did try to explain his thinking after the 3-2 defeat at the City Ground. His attempts to do so were in line with Chelsea’s performance on the night. “We have to stick together. Everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed. We need to help and we need to go through this together. We don’t leave apart anyone. [We] need to support everyone because we need everyone. item.title: Despite overall struggles, Texas QB Arch Manning leads one long drive against Texas A&M
item.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) walks the field after the Lone Star Showdown game against Texas A&M at Kyle Field on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026 in College Station, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) COLLEGE STATION - Earlier this week, Texas quarterback Arch Manning downplayed his role in the Longhorns' 17-7 win at College Station during the 2024 season . "I only played in like three plays that game," Manning told reporters. What Manning omitted was that one of those plays was a 15-yard touchdown run so it wasn't like his introduction to this rivalry was a nothingburger. But the point remains, Manning didn't play much during the Longhorns' last trip to College Station. That wasn't the case Friday. MORE: Craig Way, after 25 years as radio voice of Texas football, still 'as good as it gets' GOLDEN: The SEC must cut its ties with rules-skirting LSU and move on Manning threw for 143 yards and a touchdown as Texas recorded a 16-6 victory at Kyle Field . Sixteen of Manning's 34 passes fell incomplete and he had a deflected pass get intercepted near the end zone in the fourth quarter. The Texas offense, which posted season-low totals in yards and points, produced points on four of its 11 drives. But three of those scores were Gianni Spetic field goals. Texas A&M , however, was held to 234 yards by the UT defense. "That pick, I can't do that in that situation. I've got to run and try and get in the end zone. If not, kick the field goal," said Manning, who also led UT to a 27-17 win over Texas A&M in Austin last year. "But defense had our back all night, and they're going to continue to do that going forward." Manning did direct Texas on a 12-play drive that ended with Cam Coleman 's 3-yard touchdown catch. During an 88-yard drive that accounted for 36.4% of its offense for the evening, Manning completed all six of his attempts and also converted a 3rd-and-3 attempt with a 4-yard run. "I think we had just a really good rhythm in that drive," Texas center Connor Robertson said. View this post on Instagram A post shared by hookem.com (@hookemdotcom) Manning, Texas to meet Georgia in the SEC Championship Game For the season, Manning has thrown for 2,628 yards, 22 touchdowns and 11 interceptions while completing 64.9% of his passes. Manning will next attempt to join Paul Campbell (1949), Walter Fondren (1957), Bobby Lackey (1958) and Sam Ehlinger (2018) as the Texas quarterbacks that have led the Longhorns to a win over Georgia. Texas lost to the Bulldogs twice during the 2024 season with Quinn Ewers as its starter, and Manning was leading Texas during last season's 35-10 loss in Athens . "(Winning a conference title was) one of our goals before the season, and we're going to make the most out of it," Manning said. "Excited to go to Atlanta and play Georgia. They're kind of the standard. They've been in the SEC championship a lot of times. So we're excited for the challenge." Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman.

item.description: Luka Dončić faces criticism from NBA fans after a courtside confrontation with a Spurs supporter following the Lakers' loss in San Antonio. A courtside confrontation involving Luka Dončić and a San Antonio Spurs fan after the Los Angeles Lakers’ 99-96 loss at Frost Bank Center on Friday night drew online criticism of the superstar point guard. The spectator shoved Dončić as he walked toward the tunnel, but the exchange began moments earlier when the Slovenian guard returned to retrieve an item he had tossed toward a woman sitting courtside. Fans Show Little Sympathy for Luka Dončić After Courtside Shove The incident began as Dončić headed off the floor. The woman, seated courtside along his path, appeared to say something to him. The former Dallas Mavericks guard tossed what appeared to be his wristband toward her but then turned around to retrieve it. The man seated beside the woman had picked up the item by then. He handed it back to the six-time All-Star, but the spectator then shoved the Lakers star, prompting forward Jarred Vanderbilt and arena security to step between them. NBA Central shared video of the exchange. One fan wrote : “Can’t see how anyone can defend Luka on this. He threw his sweaty sleeve at a Spurs fan, went back to retrieve it, got shoved, and then played the victim.” Another reaction read : “He’s rattled.” A third fan commented : “Understandable response from the fan, Luka is childish.” One reply said : “Lowkey deserved that, why’d he chuck something at his … wife.” Another fan added : “You throw something at my spouse, I’m swinging.” The woman’s relationship with the spectator has not been independently established. item.description: As Liverpool prepare to make their shortest journey of the season, Alexander Isak has come a long way in a few months. The fact he is leaving Anfield, even if it is only about two-and-a-half miles to Hill Dickinson Stadium, for Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton may bode well for an increasingly impressive traveller – the misfit who has become a mainstay. Since his unhappy return to Newcastle in the season opener, when Isak was barracked by the supporters who used to adore him, the Swedish striker has played in six away games and scored in each; indeed, of his 10 goals under Andoni Iraola , only two have come at Anfield. There may be some significance in the identity of the last Liverpool player to score in six straight away matches: Mohamed Salah , and if Isak is not a direct replacement for a right winger in one respect, he has been charged with taking on the Egyptian’s mantle as Liverpool’s scorer in chief. Alexander Isak has been tasked with replacing Mohamed Salah at Liverpool (PA) Even in Isak’s decidedly difficult debut year at Anfield , Liverpool may note two-thirds of his meagre tally of three league goals came away. Since Iraola took the reins, however, Isak has become his king of the road. The head coach admitted he is unsure why. “I don’t have any clear reason, honestly,” he said. “I think the way we play is the same whether away or at home. We know we have to go for the games either way. So I think it is just a coincidence. I don’t think there is a big difference in performance away or at home.” There may, however, be a difference in the context, when opponents open up and allow a side with Liverpool’s counter-attacking pace – wingers as speedy as Bradley Barcola , Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha , and a striker as quick as Isak – to break. Isak and Bradley Barcola are part of Liverpool’s lightning-fast counter-attacking unit (Getty) “Normally you will find more spaces when you play away because teams are normally more brave and they usually press you more,” said Iraola. “Then you will find more spaces.” He has always caveated his comments about Liverpool’s excellent away form this season with reminders that he prefers to play at home. Does Isak? Much as St James’ Park loved him, explaining the sense of betrayal when he went on strike to force his exit , he was almost as potent away. In his first season at Newcastle, 2022-23, he scored five times at home, five away. In the following year, there were 15 goals on Tyneside, 10 elsewhere. item.title: Can Estudiantes end Brazil's domination of the Copa Libertadores by upsetting Palmeiras in Saturday's final in Montevideo?
item.description: Copa Libertadores final GFX - GOAL Brazil accounts for 13 of the past 16 finalists, which makes for grim reading for the rest of South American football River Plate playing Boca Juniors in the 2018 Copa Libertadores final effectively meant that Argentina couldn't lose: the country would pick up a record-extending 25th title no matter the outcome of the two-legged tie. Now, though, it's becoming increasingly difficult for anyone but Brazil to win. On Saturday evening at the historic Centenario stadium in Montevideo, Palmeiras will look to make it eight Libertadores triumphs in a row for Brasileiro Serie A sides - and 26 overall. There is a very strong Estudiantes side standing in their way, and the Argentines have already taken out Corinthians and defending champions Flamengo on their route to the final, meaning victory is by no means a given for Palmeiras. However, even if Estudiantes were to upset the odds in Uruguay, there's very little evidence to suggest that Brazil's overall dominance of Libertadores is going to end anytime soon... 'The potential is spectacular' The City Football Group (CFG) is one of several foreign groups to have invested in Brazilian clubs since a key structural rule change In a way, Brazil bossing the Libertadores is perfectly natural. The country has a population of roughly 214 million people - almost as many as the rest of South America combined (226m) - and it also boasts one of the 10 biggest economies in the world. When it came to the continental competition, though, Brazil consistently punched well below its weight. There was an impressive streak of six trophies in eight years in the 1990s, and four in a row between 2010 and 2013, but, for the most part, the country failed to turn its clear numerical and economic advantages into sustained success - until now. Brazilian clubs haven't just won the past seven Copa Libertadores; Palmeiras' participation in Saturday's game in Uruguay means that they also now account for 13 of the past 16 finalists. And why is this? Money, essentially, because Brazilian football is booming. Only Premier League clubs spent more money during the 2026 winter transfer window than their Brazilian counterparts - something that would have been unimaginable during the pandemic, when it became clear that many of the country's top-tier teams were heavily in debt. By way of a response, the government passed a law allowing clubs to become corporate entities known as ' Sociedade Anonima do Futebol ' (SAF), thus paving the way for a massive increase in external investment. Botafogo were one of several sides to ditch the sporting association membership model and their supporters were dancing in the streets when their club was acquired by John Textor's Eagle Football Holdings in February 2022. Their excitement proved well-founded, as they were celebrating again two years later when their team won a first-ever Copa Libertadores. item.description: Sarina Wiegman feature GFX - GOAL Navigating the 2027 Women's World Cup play-offs was not part of England's plan, but how Sarina Wiegman is using these unwanted fixtures could increase the Lionesses' chances of triumphing in Brazil In an ideal world, England would have spent the final two international breaks of 2026 playing friendlies against worldwide opposition, cherry-picked by Sarina Wiegman in order to best prepare the Lionesses for the 2027 Women's World Cup. Instead, a capitulation at the hands of Spain in June condemned the European champions to the play-off route, where they are having to overcome lower-ranked opponents with familiar playing styles in must-win games that it can be hard to learn much from. One could forgive Wiegman for looking at the European teams that did secure qualification in June with envy. While her England side faced a Greece team ranked outside the world's top 50 last month, Spain took on the United States in a double-header , Germany clashed with Australia and Japan, and Denmark flew to Canada. All four of those nations sit in the top 15 in FIFA's rankings. But as the old saying goes, when life gives you lemons, make lemonade. Games against Greece and Ukraine - the latter of whom England have already played twice this year, soundly beating them on both occasions - might not be stern tests against potential World Cup contenders, but Wiegman has been doing all she can to ensure there is plenty to learn from these games. Indeed, how she has approached these qualifiers so far could well give the Lionesses an even greater chance of winning the World Cup next summer. Seeking unpredictability Wiegman's England have become a little predictable in recent times, but a switch of shape in the October window indicated that could be changing For a while now, England have been quite predictable. The Lionesses almost always line up in a 4-2-3-1 shape and it's not difficult to correctly predict who will make up the majority of that XI, especially at a major tournament when the best XI is called upon. Of course, it doesn't mean they are easy to thwart and beat because of that, as their back-to-back European Championship titles show . But as Wiegman eyes World Cup glory, a little more unpredictability could go a long way. item.description: Hristo Stoichkov Bulgaria Barcelona GFX - GOAL The Bulgarian may have won the Ballon d'Or in 1994 but he was always as temperamental as he was talented Hristo Stoichkov has always been immensely proud of the fact that he shares a first name with his grandfather. But he's also long enjoyed the religious connection. During the 1994 World Cup, he mused, "With this name, there's always been one [Christ] above, and one below. The one below also performs miracles." Blasphemous? Perhaps. But also arguably accurate. Bulgaria were certainly a revelation in the United States that summer, and Stoichkov’s performances heavenly. The man was no saint during his playing days, of course, as he admitted himself. There was a rage inside him, one that drove him all the way to the pinnacle of his profession, but also resulted in him repeatedly stepping over the line. "I was raised in the middle of the street," he once told reporters in Spain. "You learn certain things there..." Discipline obviously wasn't one of them. Indeed, his career could have ended shortly after it had begun. Cruyff's Ballon d'Or promise The Dutchman clashed constantly with the Bulgarian but knew that he had the potential to become the best in the world Stoichkov was still only a teenager when he was involved in a mass brawl in the Bulgarian Cup final that saw him promptly hit with a lifetime ban. However, his suspension was reduced to a solitary month on appeal and the CSKA Sofia striker quickly set about making the most of his reprieve. In 1990, he won the Golden Shoe after netting 38 times in 30 league games, which made a number of Europe's elite sit up and take notice. Little did they know, though, that Stoichkov was already bound for Barcelona, who had moved quickly to wrap up a deal for the Bulgarian after he netted three goals across the two legs of a European Cup Winners' Cup semi-final loss to the Catalans the year before. The transfer had been carried out in such secrecy that not even Stoichkov's wife or parents knew about the pre-contract agreement he'd signed with the Blaugrana at the tail end of 1989. However, it initially looked like Barca had made a gross error of judgement in signing such a combustible character, given Stoichkov was sent off against Real Madrid in the Supercopa de Espana shortly after arriving at Camp Nou – and then, to make matters much, much worse, stamped on the foot of match referee Urizar Azpitarte before leaving the pitch. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
